newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs mixed amid cold temps in central U.S..
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs mixed amid cold temps in central U.S..

text.p: Spot U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices were mixed in light midday trade on Monday amid a cold wave in the central U.S., players said.
Frigid weather, rain and snow hit the central U.S. over the weekend and more cold was forecast Wednesday and Thursday from North Dakota to northern Texas and east to Ohio, meteorologists said.
Buyers moved up a quarter cent to 35.50 cents following a flurry of buying activity due to the cold weather. Sellers were at 35.75 cents in died-down, midday trade.
Spot propane in Mont Belvieu, Texas, was slightly lower amid a lack of news, between 34.75 cents and 35.00 cents a gallon.
The spot market was unaffected by news that NYMEX will decrease the margins on its propane contract, effective at the close of business April 8, players said.
The butane markets were slightly lower in both hubs due to a lack in demand. Belvieu normal butane traded 39.25/39.50 cents and Conway at 33.50 cents.
Meanwhile, Morocco's SOMEPI and French Primagaz group, said on Monday they signed an accord to set up a joint venture for propane gas storage and distribution worth $4.3 million.
The storage unit will be at Jorf Lasfar port, on the Atlantic Coast 200 km (125 miles) south of Morocco's financial center of Casablanca. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
